source.source_description: A tanuló által bemásolt Duolingo webes Guidebook-szöveg, 8. modul, 1–180. rész (#826–#1005).
source.note: A forrás angol kulcskifejezéseket tartalmaz, magyar fordításokat nem. A 180 egység 36 egymást követő, ötegységes blokkban ismétli a címeket és a példamondatokat; minden egység külön azonosítóval szerepel, a közös mondatanyag a phrase_sets alatt deduplikált. 195 különböző angol példamondat található benne. Három cím kifejezetten nyelvtani fókuszt nevez meg: Present Perfect Progressive, Future Perfect Progressive és Past Perfect Passive.

module.title_hu: Érvelés, következtetés, haladó igeidők és összetett társas kommunikáció

english_examples: I guess my biggest concern is the price.
Yes, it's expensive, but it'll impress the neighbors!
Why would you need a thermometer for your pet snake?
My two-year-old son accidentally made that purchase.
It was so cheap, otherwise I wouldn't have bought it.

grammar_observations.topic: otherwise + would have: implicit feltételes következmény

phrase_sets.title_source: Ask for things in a softened way
english_examples: Would you mind watering my plants while I'm out of town?
I can help out Saturday, but not Sunday.
Wait, I'm supposed to get the mail and take out the garbage?
Not if it's too much trouble.
If it's not too much to ask, could you walk the dog?
If I don't get a full refund, I'll leave you a bad review!
I can't refund your money, but I can give you store credit.
I'm never coming back, so giving me store credit is useless.
Unfortunately, you already removed the sticker.
I'm afraid it only had a two-year guarantee, ma'am.
Are you sure the manager is unavailable?
Next up, we'll hear about a dog with an amazing talent!
Let's hear how one man is helping the local deer population.
An interview with the former world champion is next!
The lifeguard jumped into the ocean and rescued the dog.
That must have taken a lot of bravery!

grammar_observations.topic: must have + past participle: múltbeli következtetés

english_examples: Jazz music dates back to the 19th century.
Before the fifties, pop music had a slower rhythm.
Electronic music became popular in the eighties.
So many great soundtracks were released in the nineties.
That album is still influential today.
The industry has been growing slightly.
What have you been researching lately?
Public opinion has been slowly changing.
Many young adults have recently been moving to the area.
Prices have been increasing gradually.

phrase_sets.title_source: Talk about how things have changed
english_examples: Nothing would have improved if we hadn't gone on strike.
Gender roles have changed a lot since then.
Half the US population lived in rural areas 100 years ago.
Over time, there have been a lot of changes in healthcare.
Compared with the nineties, the internet is faster now.

grammar_observations.topic: third conditional: would have + past participle / if + Past Perfect

english_examples: If we can't get there by halftime, it's not worth it.
Washing my jersey would bring bad luck!
We both know that's just nonsense!
Let's try to sit in the first row of the bleachers.
That's not exactly the best place to watch the game.
Personally, I don't think she made the right call.
It's clear that it was Mr. Nelson who stole the documents.
But did he realize he was breaking the law?
As a matter of fact, she's not as rich as she claims!
If he was innocent, he wouldn't have burned the evidence!
Let's remember that he might be lying.

grammar_observations.topic: cleft sentence: It was X who...
as a matter of fact: discourse marker
mixed conditional / unreal present + past result

english_examples: When I realized they stole my money, I was furious!
Do you get those awful spam calls too?
She was being dishonest the entire time.
Frankly, it's hard not to be bitter about all her lies.
This so-called "sale" is just a scam!

grammar_observations.topic: Past Continuous passive-like progressive with be: was being dishonest

phrase_sets.title_source: Discuss plans for a work party
english_examples: The break room doesn't have seating for a hundred people.
What other venues are there?
Let's do a tropical theme with beach balls and coconuts!
Her request that we serve lobster is ridiculous.
Shh, let's hear her out!
I think Oscar's suggestion sounds ideal!
She may have come in through the window.
There must be fingerprints somewhere!
The cat hair on her sleeve could be an important clue.
Considering how angry he was, I think he's guilty.
Only high heels could leave a footprint like that.
There was a strange noise, but it must have been the wind.

grammar_observations.topic: may have + past participle: múltbeli lehetőség

english_examples: Let's tell ghost stories around the campfire.
There's a famous legend about a werewolf in these woods.
No sooner had he fallen asleep than he heard a loud scream.
I'm dying to hear what happened after that!
Was he joking when he said there were killer rabbits?

grammar_observations.topic: no sooner + Past Perfect + than + Past Simple inversion

phrase_sets.title_source: Describe a move to the big city
english_examples: How are you adjusting to things?
It'll take some time to get used to my new surroundings.
The subway's the fastest way to travel.
How will you make a living in Hollywood?
Life in the big city isn't as romantic as I thought it'd be.

phrase_sets.title_source: Navigate a trip to a theme park
english_examples: Wouldn't it be more fun if we went to an amusement park?
Let's go on the roller coaster.
I refuse to go on any roller coaster that goes upside down.
It's hard to enjoy the amusement park when it's packed.
We waited in line for two hours, then the ride closed!
We have wristbands, so we can come back later.

grammar_observations.topic: second conditional: would... if + Past Simple

english_examples: Let's politely ask Mia to wash her pile of dirty dishes.
If you could take out the trash, that would be great.
Try to leave the kitchen clean for the next person.
We can divide the housework between us.
I can cook if you do the dishes.

phrase_sets.title_source: Express how certain or uncertain you are
english_examples: I'm sure you'll do great at your audition!
I think the set is supposed to look like a palace.
Chances are that people will laugh, but you never know.
I'm pretty sure this costume is going to tear on stage!
I don't feel ready for opening night.
There's no question it'll be a success!
Did you really ask my brother to prom?
They want some confirmation that we paid, like a receipt.
We'll send you a confirmation number.
You mean it costs 100 dollars just to rent a tuxedo?
Weren't we going to have dinner first?

grammar_observations.topic: weren't we going to: past plan / confirmation tag-like question

english_examples: We'd love to throw you a party before the move!
The office won't be the same without your warmth.
I'm going to miss you so much when you leave town!
We've had our differences, but I wish you the best, Kevin.
Give my regards to him when you see him.

grammar_observations.topic: Present Perfect: shared past to present

phrase_sets.title_source: Talk about your plans for a trip
english_examples: Are you planning on staying long?
I intend to be back by August.
You won't make your connection if you only have 20 minutes!
I booked a cheap hotel in order to save money.
Why are we thinking of flying when we could take the train?
Um, wasn't that my original suggestion, which you ignored?
In May, I will have been working here for thirty years!
On Monday, we will have been selling ice cream for 25 years!
By then, we'll have been negotiating the sale for months.
She'll have been spending more time in the office than away!
How long will he have been living in Florida by then?

grammar_observations.topic: Future Perfect Progressive: will have been + -ing

phrase_sets.title_source: Make plans for a Friday night
english_examples: Would you rather we went out or stayed in?
I don't mind staying in.
I guess we could go bowling.
We're not going bowling because you're too competitive!
Should we play dominoes or cards?
We can watch whichever movie you want.

grammar_observations.topic: whichever + noun embedded free relative clause

phrase_sets.title_source: Navigate transactions at a garage sale
english_examples: Has this machine ever been used, or is it new?
I wonder if any pieces are missing from this puzzle.
We were wondering if you'd be willing to negotiate.
If you give me a discount on the entire set, it's a deal.
This pot looks like it hasn't been washed in years.
It's just dusty, but it works fine.

phrase_sets.title_source: Respond to a command or request
english_examples: You're going to need to practice these exercises at home.
But I feel like a frog when I do squats.
Please don't make me do more pull-ups!
I'd honestly rather not run today.
Come on, I know you can do more push-ups!
But push-ups are so hard!

grammar_observations.topic: be going to need to: future necessity

phrase_sets.title_source: Politely decline an offer or proposal
english_examples: Would you care for any shrimp or lobster tails?
Sorry, I'm a vegetarian, but thanks anyway.
I don't feel like mingling with strangers.
Maybe some other time, but I'm just not in the mood.
Coffee sounds great, but I'm going to have to turn it down.

grammar_observations.topic: would you care for: formal offer
going to have to: future obligation

english_examples: OK, what's left on the to-do list?
The dryer has to be fixed.
The silverware needs to be cleaned or Grandma will complain.
When was the last time you dusted this shelf?
I hate household chores too, but I don't complain!
Relax, I already tidied up the patio.

grammar_observations.topic: has to be fixed: modal passive
needs to be cleaned: need + passive infinitive
when was the last time: Past Simple question

phrase_sets.title_source: Catch up with an old friend
english_examples: Look who's back in town!
How have things been going since I last saw you?
It's been a tough year, but I can't complain.
Please catch us up on your family!
Anna is expecting her first child, so I'll be an aunt soon!
It sounds like life's been good for both of us, overall.
The time of the meeting had been changed.
I thought the problem had been solved.
He was mad that he hadn't been promoted.
We hadn't been given all the information.
Had the email been sent out in time?
Hadn't that idea been suggested at the last meeting?

grammar_observations.topic: Past Perfect Passive: had been + past participle

english_examples: It's a steep trail, but it's the fastest route to the top.
We can't go scuba diving without the right gear.
Under these conditions, we'd get there sooner if we walked!
So long as we bring enough water, we won't get dehydrated.
It'd be too complicated to get there by bus, right?
I'm too tall to sleep in that tiny tent!
The American cyclist finished in fourth place.
They need to win this game to qualify for the final.
It's anticipated that a new world record will be set.
The soccer final is set to take place on Tuesday.
The Brazilian volleyball team is definitely expected to win.
He's the silver medalist in the eight hundred meters.

grammar_observations.topic: impersonal passive: it is anticipated that

english_examples: Built in 1907, the building used to be a hotel.
I'd like to draw your attention to the name of the street.
Take a look over here and you'll see some ancient pottery.
The area lost its charm when they built that huge mall.
This neighborhood in particular has an amazing history.

grammar_observations.topic: past participle clause as reduced relative/adverbial

english_examples: Couldn't aliens have secretly visited our planet?
Why would aliens want to come to Earth?
According to one theory, the city could have been an island.
I'm convinced that they're hiding something.
How did you come to that conclusion?

grammar_observations.topic: couldn't have + past participle: past possibility/deduction

english_examples: The magician won't ask me to help him on stage, will he?
I wonder which trick she'll do next.
Did the show live up to your expectations?
Could you explain to me where you hid the extra cards?
It'd ruin the magic if I told you precisely how I did it.
We used to go skateboarding every day after school.
Grandma's basement was perfect for playing hide-and-seek.
My sister and I were always getting in trouble.
I was jealous of the boy next door who had a cooler yo-yo.
Looking at these old photos makes me feel nostalgic.

grammar_observations.topic: always + Past Continuous: repeated irritating event

english_examples: I was already on my way when I saw that my pants were torn.
Sorry to interrupt, but what happened?
A bus broke down right on the train tracks!
The road was blocked, so I had to find a different route.
It all started to go wrong when a goat bit my tire.
Congratulations on everything that you have accomplished!
Graduating in three years is quite an accomplishment!
What a relief to have finally completed my thesis!
Although there were many long nights, it was all worth it.
Wishing you much luck in your new career!

source_structure.repetition_pattern: 36 egymást követő témacsoport, mindegyik 5 egységben azonos Guidebook-címet és példamondatokat ismétel.
source_structure.example_translation_policy: not_provided; do not generate or assume Hungarian translations.
source_structure.unit_indexing: All 180 course-local parts and course-wide ids are preserved individually.

source_conflicts.note: A bemásolt angol kulcskifejezésekhez nem érkezett magyar fordítás.
A 180 helyi egység 36 egymást követő ötegységes blokkban ismétli a címeket és példamondatokat. A phrase_sets 36 témacsoportot, a units mind a 180 külön részt tárolja.
